headline: The US–Iran war keeps Hormuz largely shut after Iran called the US reply 'not convincing' on 3 Nov. A Russian strike on a Zaporizhzhia aid point killed 33, and the Ebola outbreak has passed 5,300 deaths.

situations.name: US–Iran war and Gulf energy shock
situations.summary: US struck Qeshm Island on 2 Nov; Iran called the US reply 'not convincing' on 3 Nov. Record 30 ship attacks in October; Brent near $104.

situations.name: Russia–Ukraine war and NATO's flank
situations.summary: Toll from 2 Nov strike on a Zaporizhzhia aid point rose to 33; Russia fired 289 drones and 76 missiles overnight into 3 Nov.

situations.name: Super El Niño
situations.summary: ONI +2.2: drought in Australia and East Africa, record warmth and weaker carbon sinks.

situations.name: Ebola outbreak, DR Congo
situations.summary: Africa CDC counts 5,376 Ebola deaths and 10,444 cases to 2 Nov across DR Congo, Uganda and Kenya; a WHO emergency (PHEIC) since May.

situations.name: Sudan war
situations.summary: Sudan says drones killed 484 civilians from February to 27 Oct, with 97 drones used in October; no talks under way.

situations.name: Cyclone Murasu
situations.summary: Murasu crossed the Andhra Pradesh coast near Ongole early on 3 Nov and is weakening inland; 10,000 evacuated, no deaths reported.

situations.name: Energy shock feeding inflation

signals.state: The VIX was about 20.8 on 3 Nov, above the 20 Watch line, and the S&P 500 is about 3.2% below its high. On 2 Nov the Nasdaq 100 fell 1.4% into correction territory on doubts about returns on AI spending, while the S&P 500 lost 0.5% (Saxo). US midterms (3 Nov), the Bank of England (5 Nov) and payrolls (6 Nov) fall this week.
signals.for_you: Pension and investment values linked to US technology shares are swinging more than usual; volatility tends to stay elevated around elections and central-bank decisions.

signals.name: Crypto stress
signals.summary: Bitcoin 10% off its high; Binance still under stress after $6.3bn theft
signals.state: Bitcoin was near $77,600 on 3 Nov, about 10% below its 52-week high, which alone would be Normal. Watch rests on Binance, a top-10 exchange, still under stress after the FBI said North Korea stole about $6.3bn; Pyongyang denied it on 3 Nov (Euronews). Bitcoin ETFs saw about $399m of outflows and Coinbase fell 4% on 2 Nov after a downgrade citing the hack (Saxo).
signals.for_you: Crypto holdings on exchanges carry counterparty risk; exchange failures and thefts are not covered by deposit protection schemes.

signals.name: Euro-area economy
signals.summary: Euro-area GDP up 0.4% in Q3; ECB flags energy risks to growth
signals.state: Eurostat's flash estimate on 30 Oct showed euro-area GDP up 0.4% in Q3, though French output contracted. The ECB warned on 29 Oct that energy prices pose downside risks to growth, and euro-area flash PMIs (23 Oct) showed expansion slowing. Neither stagnation nor a sub-50 composite PMI is confirmed as of 3 Nov.
signals.for_you: Growth is holding up but slowing; higher energy costs are the main risk for jobs and incomes.

signals.name: China economy
signals.summary: Factory PMI back in contraction; regulators reportedly pause IPOs amid stock sell-off
signals.state: Chinese regulators told banks to pause IPOs and large share sales to steady a falling stock market, the FT reported on 3 Nov, after a 2 Nov pledge to support the capital market. The official manufacturing PMI fell to 49.3 in October (31 Oct). Q3 GDP grew 4.5%, near target, with no sign of financial contagion or capital controls as of 3 Nov.
signals.for_you: Chinese demand affects commodity prices and exporters' earnings; no direct effect on households elsewhere yet.
signals.rubric_hit: Growth near target; no defaults wave or contagion

signals.summary: RBA hikes to an 18-year high; Bank of England expected to raise rates on 5 Nov
signals.state: The Reserve Bank of Australia raised its cash rate to 4.85% on 3 Nov, its fifth rise this year, on a 6–3 vote (ABC). The Bank of England is expected to raise Bank Rate to 4% on 5 Nov, its first rise since 2023 (IG). The Fed held at 3.75–4% on 28 Oct. Policymakers face a stagflationary dilemma; no emergency move had been made.
signals.for_you: Variable mortgage and loan rates are rising in several countries; savings rates tend to follow.

signals.name: Gilt market
signals.summary: 10-year gilt yield near 5.2% ahead of an expected rate rise
signals.state: The 10-year gilt yield was near 5.2% on 2 Nov, below its October high near 19-year peaks but about 75bp higher than a year ago (Trading Economics). A Bank of England rise is widely expected on 5 Nov (Bloomberg). Auctions have been orderly as of 3 Nov.
signals.for_you: Mortgage rates track gilt yields; new fixed-rate deals remain costly.

signals.name: UK energy price cap
signals.summary: Energy cap £1,723; January forecasts range from +16% to +27%
signals.state: The Ofgem cap for October–December is £1,723 a year. Cornwall Insight's latest forecast (14 Oct) puts January at £1,999, up 16%, while Uswitch's average of supplier forecasts (30 Oct) points to about +27%. Alert is held under hysteresis until Ofgem announces the January cap by 25 Nov; European gas fell about 9% on 2 Nov.
signals.for_you: Bills are likely to rise in January; Ofgem and Citizens Advice list support schemes for households struggling with energy costs.

signals.name: NHS & respiratory
signals.summary: Flu low but GP positivity rising; COVID falling; RSV at baseline
signals.state: UKHSA's 29 Oct report (week 43) showed flu activity low overall but GP swab positivity rising to 11.0%, COVID low and falling, and RSV rising at baseline. The next report is due on 5 Nov. Resident doctors strike from 14 to 19 Nov and consultants on 25–26 Nov.
signals.for_you: Eligible people can book flu and COVID-19 vaccines via the NHS; use NHS 111 for urgent advice.

signals.name: UK strikes & disruption
signals.summary: Resident doctors strike 14–19 Nov; consultants 25–26 Nov
signals.state: The BMA has called a six-day strike by resident doctors in England from 14 to 19 Nov, and consultants will strike on 25–26 Nov unless the government commits to formal talks (ITV, 26 Oct). These are strikes in one sector, within the Watch band. No national infrastructure failure had been reported as of 3 Nov.
signals.for_you: Attend NHS appointments unless told otherwise; use NHS 111 for urgent care during strikes.
